policies.policy_name: Administrator Role Required for SLA Definition Creation
policies.description: Creating a new SLA definition must be performed by a user whose role is **Administrator**. The Administrator role has Full CRUD access across all tables, while other roles (Manager, Agent, Reporter) do not have permission to create SLA definitions.
references: | **Administrator** (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

policies.policy_name: Mandatory Fields Validation for SLA Definition
policies.description: Any request to create an SLA definition must include and validate all mandatory fields (`name`, `metric`, `target_mins`, `pause_on_pending`, `active`). If any required field is missing or invalid, the operation must be stopped.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: If a request to create an SLA definition violates any policy (e.g., insufficient role, missing mandatory fields), the assistant must halt the operation immediately and return the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.policy_name: Permission Enforcement – 403 Forbidden on Unauthorized SLA Definition Creation
policies.description: If a user whose role is not Administrator attempts to create a new SLA definition, the operation must be denied with a 403 Forbidden response indicating insufficient authority.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.policy_name: Conflict Handling – 409 Conflict on Duplicate SLA Definition
policies.description: When attempting to create an SLA definition whose `name` already exists (or any other record conflict occurs), the assistant must abort the creation and return a 409 Conflict error.
references: 409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.

policies.policy_name: Rate Limiting Policy for SLA Definition Creation
policies.description: If the SLA definition creation endpoint exceeds its allowed request rate, the assistant must pause the operation and retry using exponential backoff as defined in the policy.
references: Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.policy_name: Atomic Operation Requirement for SLA Definition Creation
policies.description: Creating a new SLA definition must be performed as a single validated operation; it cannot be combined with other actions unless using an approved batch endpoint.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.
